We present across the audited set a concise snapshot of the most impactful opportunities for enhancing machine comprehension and discovery. We found no llms‑full.txt; the file is absent from the root, not referenced in the sitemap, and no link tag points to it in the homepage head. If the site hosts a substantial content depth, we recommend adding llms‑full.txt with a text/html content type.
Not Compatible. Purchase Confidence does not apply – we found no transaction or checkout pages.

We find that the audited pages use semantic HTML well, providing machines with reliable structural cues.
The audited set shows consistent metadata patterns across pages, with no organisation‑name or canonical‑URL divergence flagged by the consistency check.

We found that https://www.contentful.com scores 94/100 in SEO, demonstrating strong optimisation for search crawlers across the audited set.  
However, across the audited set, Discovery Readiness at 39/100 and Structured Data at 61/100 reveal significant opportunities for improving machine discoverability and metadata quality.  
We invite you to prioritise enhancements in these areas to unlock greater visibility and richer machine comprehension.

We found 840 images with loading="lazy", 14 with loading="eager", and 36 without a loading attribute. The absence of the attribute means the browser will decide, which is not the same as eager loading.

The site’s SEO is excellent, scoring 94/100, which means search engines can easily surface and index its content, giving users quick access to relevant information. This strong SEO base reflects thoughtful keyword strategy, clean URLs, and consistent metadata—all of which enhance the overall user experience.

Across the audited set, we find that the experience for human visitors is strong, though page load times could be improved.

Across the audited set, machines can discover and parse content with a Discovery Readiness score of 39/100, yet they lack governance context because MX Readiness Level is 1 (Discoverable), while Structured Data Quality stands at 61/100, MX Stack Completeness at 66/100, and Pipeline Survivability at 79/100.

Across the audited set, we find a solid foundation in SEO—94/100 overall and 97/100 on content pages—and strong accessibility performance with 77/100. These strengths provide the groundwork for targeted improvements in structured data quality and consistency.

Across the audited set of 12 pages, we highlighted key opportunities for strengthening machine comprehension and discoverability, prioritising them by impact. Catalogue visibility gaps rank highest as they block downstream agent interactions, followed by discovery readiness which limits initial access, and then structured data quality and MX stack completeness.

We found a robots.txt file that permits all user agents to crawl the site, as it contains no disallow directives. The file also announces a single sitemap reference, confirming that the sitemap is publicly discoverable.

We assessed the sitemap and graded it Partial; it declares 3359 URLs, includes lastmod dates but omits changefreq and priority, which presents an opportunity to improve machine compatibility beyond Google.

We found no llms.txt at the root of www.contentful.com. Machines that query the host for a structured content index receive no description, page inventory or content policy; our recommendation diverges from the llmstxt.org specification: we recommend adding an llms.txt file with text/html content type.

We found no llms‑full.txt; it is absent from the sitemap and not referenced in the homepage head. Because our audit sampled only 12 pages, we cannot determine whether a full‑site llms‑full.txt would be useful for content‑heavy sites.
**Not Compatible for this site type. Purchase Confidence does not apply – no transaction or checkout pages were detected.**

We found that every audited page shows a truncation risk, meaning machines may receive only part of the content they need to understand.  
This could lead to incomplete indexing or inaccurate responses from LLMs and search crawlers.  
Addressing truncation—by reducing page size or ensuring full delivery—offers the greatest chance to strengthen resilience and give machines complete data.

We recorded a bare‑div ratio of 51 % on the rendered surface of the worst‑case page https://www.contentful.com/products/personalization/, meaning that more than half of the visible elements are generic divs and machines lose reliable structural context, forcing them to rely on positional inference.

We find consistent metadata patterns across the audited set, with no organisation‑name or canonical‑URL divergence flagged by the consistency check.
